title: Elon Musk suggests uploading credit card photos to Grok for AI-powered shopping, sparks security concerns
source_used: Moneycontrol (read from the pre-fetched full text of the AMP page)
key_facts: Elon Musk suggested in a post on his X account that users can shop online by uploading a picture of their credit card to the Grok chatbot, which would search the internet for the best price and place the order.
In a follow-up post Musk said he had asked Grok to research the most fun Lego Star Wars kits for young kids and order them, and attached a screenshot of the purchase.
The first post carries a reader-added context note saying xAI warns users not to put personal information in prompts, while credit card photos may contain such information.
According to that note, the Grok Bot's terms say user data and credentials may be stored in its cloud environment and that financial transactions require human review.
Several users criticised the idea as unsafe; one suggested the bot should generate its own single-use card numbers.
Moneycontrol says the exchange raised questions about how personal and financial information would be stored, processed and protected.
quote_evidence: "To buy stuff, you can just take a picture of your credit card, drop it in the chat and Grok @Bot will scour the Internet for the best deal on the item you want and order it," he wrote.
The context note stated, "xAI explicitly warns users not to include personal information in prompts, yet credit card photos may contain such information."
"I just asked Grok @Bot to research the most fun Lego Star Wars kits for young kids and order them. As easy as that," Musk wrote.
why_it_matters_hint: Giving a chatbot card details so it can buy for you is convenient, but it raises privacy and security questions that critics and a reader-added note have already pointed to.
event_date: Not stated; the article is dated 11 Oct 2026.
notes: Moneycontrol (Network18, India) wrote its own report on Musk's X posts. The article gives no date for the posts. The terms-of-service claims come from the reader-added note, quoted by Moneycontrol; we did not check xAI's terms. No breach or loss is reported.
